name: Stiff-Vector Kinetic Screen with Nonlocal-F+ Screened Frame
claimed_mechanism: The architecture splits the P7 collision by sourcing the preferred-frame response (lensing carrier, alpha_PF ~ e^-y) from a stiff u_mu vector kinetic term, which remains finite (K ~ 1) even in the Newtonian limit. The MOND dynamics (P_i=mu*DPhi) and the nonlocal F+ spatial operator are decoupled from this kinetic normalization, preventing the strong-coupling wall where e^-y -> 0 sends the propagating mode kinetic term to zero. This ensures the screened frame response vanishes (saving PPN) while the propagating kinetic structure remains healthy and finite.
predicted_weak_field: In the Newtonian limit (y >> 1), the e^-y screening suppresses the preferred-frame observable alpha_PF to zero, satisfying the Solar System constraints. The MOND momentum P_i recovers the standard Newtonian force (mu -> 1). The nonlocal F+ operator acts on the spatial derivatives of the MOND scalar, providing the correct finite lensing correction without requiring a local preferred-frame carrier that would otherwise be killed by the pincer.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is inequivalent to DC-001 (local no-frame) because it utilizes a preferred-frame carrier, albeit screened. It is inequivalent to DC-002 (AeST) because the vector coupling is explicitly screened by e^-y (not constant K_B) and the MOND realization is nonlocal F+ rather than a local 6-DOF aether. It avoids DC-010 (khronometric) by using a stiff-vector kinetic normalization that is independent of the screened PF coupling, directly addressing the P7 wound where the screening coefficient was tied to the kinetic term.
